text:
anya: FYI deploying batch-encoder to us-west2 GKE, seeing a bunch of pods stuck Pending. :eyes:
anya: kubectl describe shows FailedCreatePodSandBox with 'network plugin cni failed to set up pod' and 'failed to allocate pod IP' errors.
anya: also a lot of 'Insufficient cpu' for gpu nodes even though nodepool has GPUs; seems related to max pods per node / IP exhaustion.
mike: can you paste the kubectl get nodes and kubectl describe of one of the pending pods? which nodepool/name/zone?
anya: nodepool: gpu-encoder-highmem (2x a100-80gb), cluster: prod-usw2-gke, region us-west2. kubectl get nodes -o wide: 
```
NAME                                STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE     KERNEL-VERSION   CONTAINER-RUNTIME
gke-gpu-encoder-1-abcde             Ready    <none>   2d    1.28.10   10.132.5.12    34.120.21.3   Ubuntu 22.04 5.19.0-41       containerd://1.6.21
gke-gpu-encoder-2-fghij             Ready    <none>   2d    1.28.10   10.132.5.13    34.120.22.4   Ubuntu 22.04 5.19.0-41       containerd://1.6.21
```
anya: kubectl describe pod batch-encoder-0-xyz -n ml: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason                 Age               From               Message
  ----     ------                 ----              ----               -------
  Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  2m (x5 over 8m)  kubelet, gke-node    Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up pod "batch-encoder-0-xyz_default": failed to allocate IP: no usable IPs in range for node
```
anya: we also saw autoscaler add nodes but pods still pending. suspect alias IP / secondary range exhausted on the subnet.
mike: sounds like GKE VPC-native IP exhaustion, not GPU quota. do we have per-node IP range too small? what is node pool IP alias config?
anya: nodepool created with --cluster-secondary-range-name=pods-range-small, each node gets /28 for pods (max 14 pods), but our workload requests many small pods per node and we hit the IP cap.
kiran: yep, pods-per-node in GKE with alias IP is determined by size of the secondary range assigned to the nodepool. if it's /28 you're capped. we can either expand the secondary range, create a new nodepool with a bigger range, or request subnet additional secondary ranges.
anya: we need to increase capacity quickly — also hitting accelerator quota for A100 in region when trying to create more nodes (API returning QUOTA_EXCEEDED for compute.googleapis.com/accelerator).
mike: two things to request from cloud: 1) increase subnet secondary-range (pods) allocation for the VPC (or add another secondary range) 2) increase accelerator quota (A100 count) for us-west2. also double-check project-wide vCPU quota.
anya: I ran `gcloud compute regions describe us-west2 --project=redwood-prod` and it shows secondary ranges: pods-range-small: /20 (used heavily) but the nodepool mapping creates small per-node ranges; can we just move gpu-encoder pool to a nodepool with larger per-node allocation?
kiran: we can. but higher-level problem is we don't have an extra free secondary range to assign without requesting subnet modification from GCP. I'll open a support quota request for both the alias IP/secondary-range increase and the accelerator quota bump. need project number and exact quota numbers you want.
anya: project id: redwood-prod, project number: 123456789012. Request: accelerator (compute.googleapis.com/accelerator) from current 12 A100 -> 30 A100 in us-west2, and add one new secondary range pods-range-gpu /20 to the cluster subnet or expand existing by +/20.
mike: short-term mitigation: create a fallback nodepool with T4s (cheaper) and a larger pod CIDR per node, and add a node affinity to schedule less-latency-critical jobs there. also use spot/preemptible nodes for burst.
anya: doing that now as hotfix. scaling a new nodepool with t4-large and --max-pods-per-node=110. hoping to drain the Pending backlog.
sre-bot: autoscaler event: Added 3 nodes to nodepool gpu-encoder-fallback (preemptible-t4). timestamp=1833002205
anya: new nodepool came up, pods still Pending with same IP allocation error for some older nodepools that still pull from the exhausted secondary range.
kiran: support ticket opened: INC123456789 (GCP). Requested: 1) increase compute.googleapis.com/accelerator quota to 30 A100 in us-west2, 2) allocate new secondary range pods-range-gpu /20 and attach to subnet 'prod-vpc-usw2' so cluster can create new nodepools with larger per-node pod capacity. ETA 24-48h. I've included the cluster name and nodepool details in the ticket.
cloud-support: GCP support acknowledged INC123456789 — requested justification and expected steady-state numbers.
mike: make sure to include projected sustained A100 hours and business justification (we have reserved capacity customers + batch encoding spike). also ask for temporary burst if possible.
kiran: added justification and billing contact. GCP asked for the expected concurrency and node template; provided A100 node template and projected 80 A100-hours/day for next 2 weeks.
anya: tl;dr: short-term fallback: t4 preemptible pool is up and draining backlog. medium-term: waiting on GCP to add secondary range and A100 quota. long-term: consider Dedicated capacity for steady A100 reservations to avoid quota throttles.
mike: please follow up here when the quota changes land. also file infra runbook note about nodepool pod CIDR sizing and include a checklist to prevent small-range nodepools in prod clusters.
kiran: update: GCP increased compute.googleapis.com/accelerator (A100) in us-west2 to 30 for project 123456789012. They also provisioned a new secondary range pods-range-gpu /20 on prod-vpc-usw2. You should see ability to create nodepools with larger per-node pod ranges now.
anya: confirmed — I created gpu-encoder-largepool with the new secondary range and nodes come up with /24 per node allocations, Pending backlog cleared. :tada:
mike: awesome. leaving a follow-up ticket to discuss allocating some quota to a Dedicated pool for predictable steady load.
anya: closing the immediate incident. will add runbook note and share steps to avoid small per-node CIDRs. :white_check_mark:
